Things that made people love you, helped you get more stuff done, helped you organize everything, or basically anything that you felt was a good thing to have for any reason.
What are some must have things to help you with living in a dorm type setting?

A lock for your shit. Don't trust people right away. Keep your doors locked, too. Seriously, theft is a huge deal in dorms (at least at my school). Find a group, join a club, and hang out. If you're a germophobe, get rubber sandals to wear in the showers if they're shared.

Even if you're not a germophobe, wear shower shoes in shared showers.

Don't risk fucking up your feet for nothing.
If it is allowed, an electric kettle is great for tea, instant coffee, soup, etc. Bring an extra mug or two for friends.

If you feel the need to use weed in your dorm room (I'm not saying it's smart but a lot of people choose to anyway) invest in a good vaporizer for dry herbs, whether it's plug-in or portable. I saw a lot of kids suspended/kicked out freshman year, avoid burning things in there if you can.

Of course the best option is to just wait until you have your own place, but if you have to break the rules at least be smart about it.

I knew a couple people who used a paper towel tube full of fabric softener sheets to exhale into, and opened the window with a mini fan so any smoke from the burning joint would go outside. They also used lots of Febreeze and incense on an ongoing basis, so it wouldn't look suspicious, and also because they probably smoked on an ongoing basis.

Duct Tape. Storage bins for under your bed.

The thing that will most likely help or hurt your experience is your relationship with your roommate, though. You don't have to be BFFs, but if you get along, everything will be better.

A bowl that can go from the fridge to the microwave, preferably glass, with a sealing lid. I had one of these freshman year, and was so upset when it fell from a shelf and broke...thankfully my mom found another one and crisis was averted. I believe it was at "The Christmas Tree Store" which is really just a knicknack-type shop at the mall near their house.

Good god that sounds so gay reading it back. I'm gonna go do some pushups.
I had a shared Google Calendar with my roommate, it kept me organized and let me know when he wasn't going to be in the room.

Slow cooker. You can cook stuff while you're in class, come back and have your food ready. You can cook enough food for several meals in one go, and it comes in its own storage device (the cooking pot comes out of the cooker and you can fit it into a mini fridge with some room to spare for other food), so it's a great way to save time and not have stuff go to waste. Slow cookers are a great way to cook with cheap cuts of meat but still have them taste good.

Kettle and french press. You need caffeine, and it's cheaper in the long run to buy these items plus a container of coffee, instead of going to the coffee shop. They don't take up much space, and if you have a roommate, I'm sure they won't complain about it being on the counter since they can get a lot of use out of it as well.

Not really a thing but some advice.

At the beginning of the semester talk with everyone. And throughout the semester, when you're in your room, always leave your door open. My roommate and I always had our door open. People would drop by and chat for a few minutes every day. We became friends with most the kids in our hall. Seriously, it's the most passive way to make friends in college.
Be careful with the large items, mini fridge, TV, microwave etc. Make sure you are going to be able to pack everything into your car.

Maybe you could take some brownie mix and have a good icebreaker to make friends when you're settling in.

Things I took were things that reminded me of home. I took pillows, a cosy fleece blanket, my old teddy bear and a few posters and postcards to make my room seem more cosy and less prison like.
If you really want to accelerate getting friends, get a Gamecube with Smash Brothers. Guaranteed you'll meet more people that way.
